title: What Java4Shell Means for Your Business
content_md: Researchers at Calif used AI to uncover Java4Shell, a flaw in the software that runs Java applications. In affected applications, the vulnerability can allow attackers to run malicious code. The risk depends on how each application uses Java and how the system is exposed. Calif claims there is no universal exploit, and that specific circumstances dictates how it may be abused. Security updates are available. [2] What To Do Now Figure out what is affected. Check the applications you run yourself, including those in containers. Ask suppliers whether their products use an affected version of Java and when a fix will be available.[3] Patch affected systems promptly. Prioritize systems exposed to the internet and services your business depends on. Involve the service owner early so you can plan any restart and limit disruption.[4] Confirm the fix is running. Verify that the application is using the updated Java version. If a supplier manages the service, ask them to confirm when the fix was deployed.[5] Investigate.
